`HttpLoggingMiddleware` now logs response headers following an upgrade connection request as soon as the response is sent to the client.

## Description

A new decorator around the `IHttpUpgradeFeature` has been introduced in the `HttpLoggingMiddleware` in order to log the response headers while the middleware pipeline is still running due to the connection being upgraded. 

Fixes #31962

issue_context.title: HttpLoggingMiddleware + Websockets/Upgrade
issue_context.body: We need to verify that we either log the response correctly or disable request and response logging for websocket upgrades.
comments:
We should be able to log upgrade requests normally (Request.Body is not used for upgrades).

For upgrade responses we'll have to wrap the upgrade feature in order to get a timely notification of the upgrade and log headers. Otherwise the default logging will happen when the middleware eventually exits. No special handling is required for the body, Response.Body is not used for upgrades.

Hello, I would like to take a look at this issue but it's my first time working with this codebase and I'd appreciate some direction.

From my initial investigation, the issue seems to lie in the way AcceptWebSocketAsync() sends the response to the upgrade request, by "temporarily bypassing" the middleware pipeline.  This appears to be as designed, since also the documentation mentions the fact that the middleware pipeline should be kept running, although I'm curious to know why it was designed this way. 

From a pure speculative point of view, what I expected to happen is something like: 

- AcceptWebSocketAsync() should accept a delegate that handle the messages inside the WebSocket that will eventually be established

- The 101 response is sent using the usual way, by short circuiting the middleware pipeline

- The WebSocket "upgrades" the connection and is tied to it (so it should not be disposed or reused) and not to the request through the HttpContext.  

I'd like to hear your thoughts about this. I surely have missed a lot of nuances, and I'm also curious to know if there is a easier way to handle this as @Tratcher mentioned that a possible solution is to "wrap the upgrade feature". 

Thank you

See here:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/999d3d0af1194a8d59fd4d0a56db036a3bc7e7f2/src/Middleware/HttpLogging/src/HttpLoggingMiddleware.cs#L138-L151
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/999d3d0af1194a8d59fd4d0a56db036a3bc7e7f2/src/Middleware/HttpLogging/src/ResponseBufferingStream.cs#L123-L133

It looks like this is only triggered when response body logging is enabled. Otherwise it logs after `next()`:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/999d3d0af1194a8d59fd4d0a56db036a3bc7e7f2/src/Middleware/HttpLogging/src/HttpLoggingMiddleware.cs#L162-L166

For WebSockets you'd add a wrapper for `IHttpUpgradeFeature.UpgradeAsync` kindof like how `IHttpResponseBodyFeature` is wrapped here.
Thank you, understood. I'll work on it.
